newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says 1996 trade surplus may break record.
newsitem.headline: France says 1996 trade surplus may break record.

text.p: France's 1996 trade surplus may exceed the 100 billion franc record set last year, deputy finance and trade minister Yves Galland said on Friday.
Galland was speaking at a news conference to present trade data for June, which he called "entirely satisfactory".
France had a seasonally adjusted trade surplus in June of 9.7 billion francs compared with a revised surplus in May of 11.2 billion and a surplus of 8.5 billion in June 1995.
The cumulative surplus for the first six months of 1996 rose to 53.4 billion francs from 52.9 billion francs for the same period last year.
"Looking at these data we can hope for a record trade surplus in 1996," Galland said.
Second half trade data should include the sale of 46 Airbus planes, compared with 30 sold between July and December of 1995.
